surface_form_payload.question_text: Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent: start up FWKO V-001 in a controlled way, with the bypass opened as the start-up/commissioning procedure requires. Deviation (guideword Error): start-up without opening the bypass. This is a single human omission during a non-routine transient. Frequency C (Casual): the only documented safeguard is the commissioning procedure. It is an administrative measure that fails in the same way as the cause (a procedural error), so it earns only partial credit. No engineered or independent protection layer is documented, and start-ups recur over the facility life. Severity II (Moderate): the stated consequence is limited to possible internal damage to the vessel and accessories. This is repairable asset damage, with no stated injury, loss of containment, or environmental impact. Matrix II x C gives M. The class is fairly robust: the neighboring plausible cells III x C and III x B also give M; only II x B gives L. Recommendations: add an explicit bypass line-up verification step, with sign-off or an independent check, to the start-up and commissioning procedures. Train operators on the start-up sequence. Evaluate bypass-position indication or a start-up permissive.
safeguards_considered: Commissioning procedure (CASE-06): a preventive administrative control. It gets only partial credit because the initiating cause is itself an error in carrying out the start-up procedure.
The packet documents no engineered or independent safeguards, such as bypass-position indication or permissive, pressure or differential-pressure alarm, or relief protection. None were credited.

Recommended, not credited: an explicit bypass-open verification step with sign-off or a second-person check in the start-up/commissioning procedure; a valve line-up checklist; operator training; evaluation of bypass-position indication or a start-up permissive.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Defines the node scope as V-001 and associated lines. The bypass named in the cause is presumed to lie within this node.
The element Start/Stop Procedures with guideword Error frames the deviation as a human or procedural error during a non-routine operation.
The deviation is an error in FWKO start-up procedures. Start-up is a transient mode in which omissions are credible.
The cause is a single omission (bypass not opened) with no documented engineered barrier. This supports a mid-scale frequency.
The consequence is limited to possible internal damage to V-001 and accessories, which is asset damage. This supports Moderate severity.
The only safeguard is the commissioning procedure. It is administrative and not independent of the procedural-error cause, which limits how far frequency can be reduced.

uncertainty_notes: The packet does not state what the bypass serves (vessel bypass or control-valve bypass). It also does not state the damage mechanism (flow surge, differential pressure on internals, or pressure transient). Severity is rated only on the stated consequence.

The packet does not give the number of start-ups (commissioning only, or repeated restarts after shutdowns and maintenance). It also does not say whether supervision or checklists are used. If start-ups are rare and independently verified, frequency could be B, which with severity II gives L.

The packet does not define the severity scale (repair cost or downtime thresholds). If the internal damage means a long outage, vessel entry, or knock-on loss of level or separation control, severity III is plausible. Risk would remain M at frequency B or C.

Overpressure and loss of containment are not stated in the packet and were not assumed. If a blocked-in or overpressure mechanism exists, it should be assessed as a separate scenario with potentially higher severity.

The subjective probability is a judgment aid only; it is neither a matrix input nor derived from data. It is about 20% that at least one start-up without opening the bypass damages V-001 internals or accessories over the facility operating life.
